building.local_amendments_note: Indianapolis writes no building code of its own: Revised Code Section 536-801 incorporates the state Commission's rules by reference, with later state amendments, and says a variance may be granted only by the state Commission. Chapter 536 holds the city's administrative rules (permits, exempt work, inspections, fees).

permit.exempt_list_quote: Sec. 536-201. When building permits required; enforcement. (a) Permit required. Except for construction specified in subsections (b) and (c), it shall be unlawful for a person, partnership or corporation to engage in any construction or demolition or removal of structures unless a written building permit issued by the division of construction and business services describing the activity has been obtained [...] (c) Exemptions for commercial construction. With respect to Class 1 structures, permits specified in subsection (a) shall not be required for: (1) Ordinary maintenance and repair of a structure where the work does not reduce performance or create additional safety or health risks as defined in section 536-111(i); (2) Installation, maintenance and repair of storm windows and other exterior windows designed and used as protection against severe weather; (3) Attachment of window awnings to exterior walls where the awnings project not more than forty-eight (48) inches from any wall; (4) Painting, papering and similar finish work; (5) Installation of movable cases, counters and partitions not over sixty-nine (69) inches high; (6) Erection or installation of temporary motion picture, television and theater stage sets and scenery; (7) Installation of thermal insulation; [...] (16) Ordinary maintenance and repair of building equipment where the work does not reduce performance or create additional safety or health risks; [...] (19) Replacement in kind of piping in a plumbing system [...]; (20) Replacement of appliances, fixtures, traps and valves in a plumbing system; [...] (25) Repair or replacement of an electrical meter base, riser, and weather head where such equipment is not relocated or upgraded [...]. (G.O. 132, 1995, § 2; G.O. 168, 1999, § 1; G.O. 1, 2002, § 1; G.O. 3, 2009, § 23; G.O. 41, 2016, § 2; G.O. 38, 2025, § 1)
permit.note: Item (5) names 'movable cases, counters and partitions not over sixty-nine (69) inches high'. It does not name toilet partitions or compartments, and the list does not say whether stalls anchored to the floor, wall or ceiling count as 'movable' or how the 69 inches is measured. Item (1) exempts 'ordinary maintenance and repair', defined in Section 536-111 as work 'securing the original level of performance' that does not alter 'functional features of an existing structure'; the definition's examples (replacing broken glass, patching a roof) do not include partitions. 'Construction' in Section 536-111 includes 'work undertaken to alter, remodel, rehabilitate, or add to any part of a Class 1 or Class 2 structure'. The same wording, with a six foot limit, is in the state's filing exemption (675 IAC 12-6-4(b)(5)(B), state pack). An older city print of the same list (Building Standards and Procedures, effective January 1, 2018) reads the same for items (1) to (21).
permit.definition_quote: Ordinary maintenance and repair means construction commonly accomplished in or on an existing structure for the purpose of preventing deterioration or performance deficiencies, maintaining appearance, or securing the original level of performance. [...] Ordinary maintenance and repair shall not include any construction that alters the prior or initial capacity, performance specifications, type of required energy or functional features of an existing structure or building equipment.

restrooms_city.note: No Indianapolis-Marion County ordinance or code amendment on single-user restroom signs or shared all-gender rooms was found (one web search; Chapter 536 as read has none, and Section 536-801 leaves building rules to the state). The only local item found was a 2016 news report of a councillor wanting to discuss gender-neutral restrooms, with no ordinance. The full Revised Code on Municode could not be opened, so this is 'none found', not 'none exists'.

public_wage.why_null: The active federal building determination for Marion County (IN20260002, modification 2, the only active Building determination found for the county in sam.gov's search) lists no general carpenter classification that covers Marion County. Its carpenter entries are: millwrights in Marion County ($39.10 + $25.95), and carpenters and drywall hangers in other counties only (Zone 2: Boone, Fountain, Hendricks, Monroe, Montgomery and Morgan, $35.55 + $24.21; Zone 4: Blackford, Delaware, Jay and Madison, $37.54 + $24.90). Modifications 0 and 1 are the same on this point. A carpenter rate on a Marion County project would be added after award under 29 CFR 5.5(a)(1)(iii). The neighbouring-county rate is not used on the page.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Indianapolis job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material and see the Indiana rules that apply.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Indianapolis offices, schools, hospitals and distribution centers, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Indiana's building rules set the number of toilets by how many people use the building, and Indianapolis applies them unchanged. The table below shows what that means.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Indianapolis requires a permit for construction work in a commercial building unless the work is on the city's exempt list. The list covers ordinary maintenance and repair, painting and similar finish work, and movable cases, counters and partitions not over 69 inches high. It doesn't name toilet partitions, so ask the Indianapolis Department of Business and Neighborhood Services whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.confirm_office: the Indianapolis Department of Business and Neighborhood Services
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, the building rules count an office at one person per 100 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 20. Your architect or the Indianapolis Department of Business and Neighborhood Services sets the final number.
page.install_rule: Contractors doing construction work in Indianapolis must be listed with the Department of Business and Neighborhood Services. Beech Grove, Lawrence, Southport and Speedway are excepted from the city's rule. Indiana has no state license for general or specialty contractors for work like partition installation. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: A contractor working in Indianapolis must be listed with the city's Department of Business and Neighborhood Services.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** Indiana repealed its wage law for public construction in 2015 and state law now stops public agencies from setting their own wage scales, so a required wage applies only on federally funded projects. The federal wage list for building work in Marion County has no rate for carpenters. A rate for a trade that isn't listed is added after the contract is awarded, so ask the agency paying for the project.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 7% in Indianapolis. Indiana's sales tax is one rate for the whole state.
page.buyers_extra: - **Stadiums, arenas and convention halls:** HDPE or phenolic where event crowds and washdown are hard on stalls.
sources: - Codes Indianapolis enforces: Revised Code of the Consolidated City and County, Chapter 536 (Buildings and Construction), Section 536-801, which incorporates the Indiana Fire Prevention and Building Safety Commission's rules (675 IAC Article 13, Indiana Building Code, and Article 16, Indiana Plumbing Codes) with later amendments, and Section 536-121 (enforced by the Department of Business and Neighborhood Services). Read on a secondary copy, [Zoneomics, Indianapolis code, Chapter 536](https://www.zoneomics.com/code/indianapolis-IN/chapter_3); official text: [Municode](https://library.municode.com/in/indianapolis_-_marion_county/codes/code_of_ordinances?nodeId=TITIIPUORSA_CH536BUCO). Editions in effect: [Fire Prevention and Building Safety Commission rules](https://www.in.gov/dhs/boards-and-commissions/fpbsc-rules). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Toilet counts are the state's in Indianapolis: Section 536-801 of the Revised Code adds no fixture rules and leaves variances to the state Commission ([Zoneomics copy](https://www.zoneomics.com/code/indianapolis-IN/chapter_3)). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Work exempt from a permit in Indianapolis: Revised Code Section 536-201(a) and (c), items (1), (4) and (5), with the definitions of construction and ordinary maintenance and repair in Section 536-111, read on a secondary copy ([Zoneomics](https://www.zoneomics.com/code/indianapolis-IN/chapter_3)); an earlier city print: [Building Standards and Procedures of the Consolidated City of Indianapolis, effective January 1, 2018](https://interactive.wthr.com/pdfs/IndyBuildingStandardsAndProcedures.pdf). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Sales tax rate: Indiana Department of Revenue, [County Tax Rates: Businesses](https://www.in.gov/dor/i-am-a/business-corp/county-tax-information/) ("The sales tax for the entire State of Indiana is 7%.") and [Tax Types](https://www.in.gov/dor/about/news-publications/our-team/tax-types/). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Federal wage rates for building work in Marion County: [federal wage determination IN20260002, modification 2, May 18, 2026](https://sam.gov/wage-determination/IN20260002/2), which lists millwrights but no carpenter classification for Marion County. Checked 2026-11-24.
page.official_names: - The rules by their official names: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design; 2014 Indiana Building Code (675 IAC 13-2.6, 2012 International Building Code with Indiana amendments, effective December 1, 2014), Chapter 11 with ICC A117.1-2009 as amended by 675 IAC 13-2.6-13; 2012 Indiana Plumbing Code (675 IAC 16-1.4, 2006 International Plumbing Code with Indiana amendments, effective December 24, 2012); both enforced in Indianapolis through Section 536-801 of the Revised Code of the Consolidated City and County, without local amendments; Revised Code Section 536-201 for work exempt from permits; NFPA 286 for HDPE.
